title: Chicago pianists: Clarence Jones, Dave Payton, Teddy Weatherford, Earl Hines
summary: They discuss other Chicago pianists and where they worked.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Who were considered the very best in Chicago then? He was. I mean, otherwise, were there other people... Somebody told me, by the way, that Clarence Jones, as if he was something special. Was he very good? Clarence Jones? Jones, yes.
One of the best there ever was.
I never got to meet him or know him.
Yes. How was Dave Payton? Was he pretty good? Very good.
Very good, but he wasn't the musician. You see, Dave Payton worked at the Grand Theatre for Gibbs, and then he worked at the Regal.
Regal, I know. That's when I knew him. I didn't know him, but I never knew him very well.
And then he started working on the nightclubs and things like that.
Kenny Weatherford was supposed to be a good pianist here once. He was. Something like Earl Heinstein. He was.
But Earl was different from all of them. stuff
